units.translation: But when I recalled the unrelenting toils.
better
better.
after which words one verse has fallen out.
You are far better at advising others than yourself.
The gods below are better at taking than at letting go.
Never consider stubbornness better than good counsel.
For having received him returning from the expedition, having gained most things better for her joy,
It is better to sit near the hill.
Nevertheless it is better — never to forget this strength.
to neglect, to be careless
I do not care for, I neglect.
And learn to be careless (I wrote this for μὴ ἀμελεῖν [not to be careless], which is in M, but with the alpha erased).
to be careless of these gods (here too and at 773 M has μὴ ἀμελεῖν [not to be careless])
Think, as one fearing, not to be careless of the gods.
This kindly ordinance does not neglect Cypris.
blameless
blameless.
Hurry, so that I may be blameless in respect of time.
a blameless end (thus Hermann, previously ἀμέμπτων [of blameless ones]) in all things.
blamelessly
without reproach.
having acted blamelessly.
blameless
blameless.
Thus Hermann for ἀμομφητονδετινατον λόγον [a blameless ... word].
She bore a blameless child.
For wealth at least is blameless.
They stretched out this blameless word.
a blameless ... word
blamelessness, freedom from reproach
no blame.
Correctly the scholiast: μέμφονται δὲ οἱ φίλοι αὐτῶν τὸν διαλλακτῆρα σίδηρον ὡς μηδετέρῳ χαρισάμενον [their friends blame the reconciling iron as having favored neither side].
But for friends there is no blamelessness in the reconciler.
their friends blame the reconciling iron as having favored neither side
not wrathful, without anger
not causing anger.
a storm not arisen without the anger of the gods.
With good repute and a report not causing anger.
a storm of the Achaeans not without the anger of the gods
without anger
without anger.
ἀμηνίτοις [without anger] Auratus.
Since Zeus placed you without anger to be a partner in the lustral waters of the house.
without anger
to be at a loss, to be without resources
I am without counsel.
so as to be at a loss where to turn.
I am at a loss — where to turn my resourceful thought.
For now I am at a loss amid riddles and dark oracles.
But I am at a loss for the end.
But I am at a loss.
And Zeus, seeing you at a loss, pities you.
helpless, without resources
helpless, without counsel.
which can by no means be escaped or averted.

about which the scholiast on Eur. Or. 25: ἡ γὰρ Κλυταιμνήστρα χιτῶνα ΰφανεν (Αγαμέμνονι) οὔτε ταῖς χερσὶν οὔτε τὴ κεφαλῇ ἔκδυσιν ἔχοντα [for Clytemnestra wove a tunic (for Agamemnon) that had no way out for the hands or the head].
Often in troubles the helpless one (I wrote this for ἀμήχανον [helpless]) — he raises up.
with helpless miseries.
[with helpless misfortunes.]
For he is clever at finding ways out of helpless situations.
a helpless pasture of misery.
a helpless contrivance (Nauck: τέχνημα [artifice]) and hard to escape,
for Clytemnestra wove a tunic (for Agamemnon) that had no way out for the hands or the head
helplessly
without help or counsel.
See the son of Atreus in the rest helplessly (should be written ἀμαχάνως [helplessly]) situated.
these things are helpless (thus Butler for ἐμοί [to me]).
undefiled, pure
unpolluted.

Thus I emended what is read in M: γναπτόμενοι δ᾽ ἁλὶ δεινὰ — [carded by the sea, terrible things —], about which I have said more in Philologus vol. 13 p. 480. It is absurd for ἀμιάντου [undefiled] to be said without ἁλός [of the sea], which could not be omitted, but to add ἁλί [by the sea] where it was not needed.
